notes: Company summary: mid-stage legal-tech platform providing contract search, precedent retrieval, and matter-level knowledge graphs. Heavy enterprise customers (top-50 law firms).

Current infra: hybrid model; index store on-prem for PII, cloud vector cache for latency-sensitive queries. ~150M vectors, 1536-dim embeddings, cold storage on S3-compatible object store behind VPC gateway.

Primary project: migrate from vendor A embeddings + in-house BM25-reranker to an evals-driven pipeline (new embedding model + lightweight transformer reranker). Goal: reduce cost-per-query by 35% while meeting or improving quality (MRR & top-1 precision).

Scale and perf targets: 400 QPS peak (query mix 60% short chat-like, 40% long doc search); 95th percentile end-to-end latency target 200ms (aiming for <=120ms for top-k single-shot queries; reranker budget 60-100ms).
Cost sensitivity: procurement requires 30–40% unit-cost reduction or a demonstrable ROI via caching/batching recommendations. Dedicated/Fleet sizing under review.

Quality requirements & evals: team provided 12k labeled pairs and 3k synthetic hard negatives. Acceptance criteria: no drop >1.0% absolute in MRR@10 vs baseline, preference for +2% lift. Regression alerting must be in place for nightly eval runs.

Rollout plan discussed: A/B experimentation for 2 weeks (50/50) on low-risk customers, canary rollout 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback if eval metrics breach threshold. SE recommended Canary guardrails + automated eval hooks in Redwood Console.
Technical concerns noted on call: reranker tail latency variance under continuous batching, KV cache warm-up for long documents, and vector index compaction I/O during peak rebuilds.

Security/compliance notes: must pass SSO/SAML integration, provide audit logs for embeddings + search queries, and ensure no PII leaves on-prem index. Legal team flagged retention controls and explicit deletion APIs.
